questions.stem: A 27-year-old businessman presented with a 14-day history of watery loose stool, bloating, and some intermittent abdominal pain. Symptoms had started on the day of his return from a 9-day business trip to Thailand. He also noted fat droplets in his stools. He had stayed in a hotel and only ventured out of the hotel on one occasion. He had enjoyed the local food served during his trip and was fond of fresh fruit, salads, and iced drinks.
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely etiologic agent?
questions.explanation: Giardia spp. The exposure to iced drinks even in a hotel setting along with fresh salads, likely to have been washed in local water, is suggestive of Giardia infection. The development of symptoms with watery diarrhea at 7–14 days is typical of Giardia infection.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 6 Q8

questions.question: Father and child all present with watery diarrhea. Shown a poor-quality picture. [image-based question: poor-quality picture, presumably of organism/trophozoite on microscopy]

parts.text: A) What is the causative organism?
B) Treatment?

cohort_answer.text:
Giardia lamblia OR Giardia duodenalis OR Giardia intestinalis
First choice is: Tinidazole 2g PO x 1 dose. Or Nitazoxanide 500mg PO BID x 3 days. Alternative: Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x 5-7 days

questions.question: Q75 (2010 PM). Father and children all present with watery diarrhea. Shown a poor quality picture, probably Giardia. [image-based question: microscopy image, likely Giardia]

parts.text: A) What is the causative organism?
B) Treatment?

cohort_answer.text: A) Giardia lamblia. B) First line: Tinidazole 2g PO x1 or Nitazoxanide 500mg PO BID x3 days; Alternate: Metronidazole 500mg PO BID x5-7 days.

questions.question: Name the most likely pathogen for the following scenarios.

parts.text: AML patient with central venous catheter with sepsis and haemorrhagic bullous skin lesions. The aspirate is growing a GPR.
Asplenic patient with sepsis after dog bite.
Necrotizing scalp infection after swimming.
CVID patient with chronic abdominal pain and diarrhea.

questions.model_answer: a) AML patient with CVC, sepsis, hemorrhagic bullous lesions, GPR growing on aspirate: most likely Bacillus cereus (or consider Clostridium species) - hemorrhagic bullae in neutropenic host with CVC and gram-positive rod strongly suggests Bacillus cereus bacteremia. b) Asplenic patient with sepsis after dog bite: Capnocytophaga canimorsus. c) Necrotizing scalp infection after swimming: Aeromonas hydrophila (freshwater exposure) - consider Vibrio vulnificus if saltwater exposure. d) CVID patient with chronic abdominal pain/diarrhea: Giardia lamblia.

questions.question: What is the most likely bug in the following scenarios?

parts.text: Dog bite -> sepsis
Scalp wound cellulitis from fresh water
CVID with bloating and diarrhea
CA patient with bullous skin lesions and Gram stain showing GPBs

cohort_answer.text: 1) Capnocytophaga canimorsus. 2) Aeromonas. Others: Burkholderia, Edwardsiella, Plesiomonas, Pseudomonas. Salt water: Vibrio, Shewanella, Erysipelothrix. 3) Giardia. 4) Clostridium septicum (w/o trauma), due to the malignancy

questions.question: PM 14. What is the most likely organism to the species level in the following situations? AML with CVC and hemorrhagic bullae with GPB? (1); Fresh water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis (1); CVID on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea (1); Post splenectomy patient who gets sepsis following a dog bite (1)

parts.text: AML with CVC and hemorrhagic bullae with GPB?
Fresh water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis
CVID on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea
Post splenectomy patient who gets sepsis following a dog bite

cohort_answer.text: Clostridium septicum (in immunocompromised can cause gas gangrene without trauma, differentiating from C. perfringens; translocates from GI to hematogenous spread to skin; associated with colorectal CA). Aeromonas hydrophila (fresh water). Giardia lamblia/duodenalis. Capnocytophaga canimorsus.

questions.question: Name the bug: AML - fever hypotensive bullae on legs and GPB and gram stain; CVID with diarrhea and bloating; Asplenia patient with fever and hypotension

parts.text: AML - fever hypotensive bullae on legs and GPB and gram stain
CVID with diarrhea and bloating
Asplenia patient with fever and hypotension

cohort_answer.text: AML case: Clostridium septicum. CVID: Giardia lamblia. Asplenic: Pneumococcal sepsis; Meningococcal sepsis; Salmonella; Capnocytophaga; H. influenzae. Freshwater swimmer: Aeromonas spp.

questions.question: Infection risk in CVID

parts.text: CVID patient with GI discomfort, bloating and diarrhea? (organism)
Infections at risk in CVID

cohort_answer.text: A) Giardia lamblia. B) Pulmonary: H influenzae, S. pneumo, Staph, Mycoplasma, enterovirus (chronic lung disease: bronchiectasis, pulmonary fibrosis with granulomas, acute/chronic bronchitis). H&N: rhinosinusitis, otitis media, conjunctivitis. GI: acute infectious diarrhea (norovirus, Campylobacter, cryptosporidium, Giardia, Salmonella, H pylori, IBD). UTI: mycoplasma/ureaplasma. Joints: septic arthritis. Skin: herpes zoster, molluscum. CNS: meningitis. Systemic: bacterial sepsis especially encapsulated organisms.
